MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  JULY 12, 2016

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:02 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
City Council Member Absent:  Mitchell, Schmitz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead

Others Present:  Jeff Romanelli, Park and Activities Commission
  Victor Yoo, Planning Commission

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PRESENTATION BY LOS ANGELES COUNTY SUPERVISOR DON KNABE

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN commented that it was an honor to recognize Supervisor
  Knabe for his contributions to the City and provided a list of his many
  accomplishments over the last 20 years.

  Supervisor Knabe commented that his goal was to meet with all the cities in his
  district and thank them for their support. He also thanked Rebekah Kim, his
  Field Deputy, for her assistance over the years.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN commented that Supervisor Knabe has been a
  strong supporter of contract cities. He further commended Supervisor Knabe
  for his support of the Safe Surrender Program and his work on behalf of the
  victims of child sex trafficking.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 28, 2016

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 28, 2016 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JULY 12, 2016
 B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – JUNE AND JULY

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 57054 THROUGH 57076 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $261,292.61; SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 060116 THROUGH 060316;
  56883 THROUGH 56904; 56885 (VOID); 56944 THROUGH 56968, 56963
  (VOID); 56998 THROUGH 57035; 062416; 56998 (VOID) IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $601,486.21 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF
  $862,778.82 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Schmitz

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE ITEM A.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

  NONE

10.  OLD BUSINESS (Taken out of order)

A.  PERS UNFUNDED ACCRUED LIABILITY

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to take necessary steps to
  pay off the Pre-2013 UAL prior to July 15, 2016 and increase street capital
  investment to $1,000,000 annually for three years by utilizing available fund
  balance.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN explained the PERS process and the resulting unfunded
  liability.

  City Manager Prichard noted that by paying a lump sum, the City will save
  approximately $2,000,000 in imputed interest costs.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted her appreciation to Administrative Services
  Director Whitehead and Mark Young, KNN Consultant, for their work on this
  issue. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN thanked Mr. Young as well.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO PAY OFF THE PRE-2013 UAL PRIOR TO JULY 15, 2016 AND
  INCREASE STREET CAPITAL INVESTMENT TO $1,000,000 ANNUALLY
  FOR THREE YEARS BY UTILIZING THE AVAILABLE FUND BALANCE.

  AYES:  Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Schmitz
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JULY 12, 2016
 B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 18-16; PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  (PSA) TO RETAIN TRANSTECH TO CONDUCT A HYDROLOGY STUDY FOR THE
  DAPPLEGRAY LANES BRIDLE TRAILS, INCLUDING JUNE’S TRAIL, AT PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Professional Services
  Agreement with Transtech in the amount of $31,300.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He
  noted that there will be a few minor revisions to the agreement language subject
  to City Attorney approval. He further noted that he spoke with Jerry Gliksman,
  who represents the Dapplegray area, and explained how this study will affect the
  neighborhood. Additionally, he stated that in discussions with Transtech, they
  agreed to lower their price.

  Kirk Retz, 18 Dapplegray Lane, commented that there are several engineers in the
  Dapplegray Lanes Property Owners Association who have long-term knowledge of
  this issue. He reminded the COUNCIL of the opportunity to include residents’
  input in this project.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  TRANSTECH IN THE AMOUNT OF $31,300 SUBJECT TO REVIEW BY THE
  CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Schmitz

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF JUNE 27, 2016

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF JUNE 27, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  POLITICAL REFORM ACT REPORTING REQUIREMENTS/CITY CONFLICT OF
  INTEREST CODE

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2371 which will
  adopt by reference the current Fair Political Practices Commission Standard
  Model Conflict of Interest Code and designate positions required to submit
  Statements of Economic Interest.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2371.

  AYES:  Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Schmitz

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2371 by title only.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JULY 12, 2016
 C.  AWARD OF BID – GUARDRAIL REPLACEMENT ON RANCHVIEW ROAD

  Recommendation: That the City Council award the bid to Act 1 Construction for
  removal and installation of the guardrail on Ranchview Road in the amount of
  $33,650.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO AWARD THE BID TO ACT 1 CONSTRUCTION FOR REMOVAL AND
  INSTALLATION OF THE GUARDRAIL ON RANCHVIEW ROAD IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $33,650.

  AYES:  Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Schmitz

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 18-15 (PENINSULA POINTE); APPLICANT: SCOTT
  DARNELL ON BEHALF OF SRE DCM PV, LLC; LOCATION: 27520 HAWTHORNE
  BOULEVARD

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the public hearing on the
  Project approvals (Ordinance and Resolutions); 2) Take public testimony; 3)
  Discuss the issues; 4) Approve for introduction Ordinance No. 706 amending the
  zoning designation of 27520 Hawthorne Boulevard from Commercial-Office (C-0)
  to Commercial-General (C-G)/Mixed Use Overlay District of the City’s Zoning; and
  5) Continue the public hearing to the City Council meeting of July 26, 2016.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material). She
  listed the entitlements required.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Senior Planner Naughton noted that the
  smaller facilities of this type are pre-empted by state law as local jurisdictions
  cannot regulate parking requirements, number of employees, etc.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF referred to concerns expressed by a Rancho Palos Verdes
  resident in regards to parking. Senior Planner Naughton explained the physical
  constraints of the existing structure.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired about the parking plan and asked if those who are
  affiliated with this facility should not park on Ravenspur Drive.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that visitors would need to be informed as to
  where they can park.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN commented that he would like to see a condition
  added to provide for monitoring of the operation. He further noted that the City
  should be fair to those Rancho Palos Verdes residents who will be affected by this
  decision.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that the CUP would be the proper mechanism as
  far as regulating conditions which could include an annual review.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF referred to those residents who are currently utilizing the
  parking lot overnight and asked if there would be a way to work out an
  arrangement with the Applicant. Planning Director Wahba responded that this is
  private property and the decision would be left to the property owner.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that he believes in a good neighbor policy, but to
  keep in mind that the existing apartment complex in Rancho Palos Verdes has
  been under parked for many years and does not meet standard. He further noted
  that since the Applicant does meet and exceeds standard in Rolling Hills Estates,
  it would be inappropriate to deny his property rights.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JULY 12, 2016
   MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  Douglas Pancake, Architect, thanked the Planning staff for being professional and
  prompt. He then introduced Claire Jagger, Traffic Consultant, and Eric Dudek,
  Specialist in Senior Living. He provided a Power Point presentation and explained
  his extensive experience with senior living.

  Naola Richardson, 5718 Ravenspur Drive, Unit #301, Rancho Palos Verdes,
  commented that she does not support this project and noted several of her
  concerns.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that traffic would actually be reduced because the
  current offices would no longer be at that location.

  In regards to Ordinance No. 706, MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted his concern
  for the Peninsula’s aging population. He noted that reasonable conditions should
  alleviate potential problems. Because this is the first assisted living facility in the
  City, he expressed concern about the accuracy of the findings in the studies upon
  which the COUNCIL’S decision would be made.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN further noted that the City’s revenue sources are
  minimal and appropriate replacement for lost revenue should be considered.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO: 1) INTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 706; 2) CONTINUE RESOLUTION
  NOS. 2372, 2373 AND 2374; 3) DIRECT STAFF TO INCORPORATE
  ANNUAL MONITORING IN THE CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT (CUP); AND 4)
  CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING TO THE NEXT MEETING OF JULY 26,
  2016.

  AYES:  Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell, Schmitz

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 706 and Resolution Nos. 2372, 2373
  and 2374 by title only.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

A.  City Attorney Davis followed up with a brief discussion regarding possible ways to
  increase revenue. He noted that the COUNCIL might want to set a policy that will
  address this issue.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF reported that an Environmental Advisory Committee
  meeting took place where discussion included water conservation measures and
  recommendations from Cal Water.

B.  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF reported that she attended a COG Steering Committee
  meeting and the update of the Community Choice Aggregation was discussed.
  She further reported on the Senior Services Working Group.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JULY 12, 2016
 13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  DESIGNATION OF VOTING DELEGATES AND ALTERNATES FOR THE LEAGUE
  OF CITIES ANNUAL CONFERENCE – OCTOBER 5-7, 2016 – LONG BEACH

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN DEFERRED THIS ITEM TO THE NEXT MEETING
  OF JULY 26, 2016.

B.  APPOINTMENT OF COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ TO MEDIAN LANDSCAPE
  SUBCOMMITTEE

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL

  TO APPOINT COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ TO THIS SUBCOMMITTEE.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  NONE

15.  ADJOURNMENT  IN MEMORY OF THE FIVE FALLEN DALLAS POLICE
  OFFICERS WHO WERE KILLED IN THE LINE OF DUTY AND HONORING THE
  SEVEN OTHER OFFICERS AND STAFF FROM THE DALLAS POLICE
  DEPARTMENT WHO WERE INJURED ON JULY 7, 2016

  At 8:58 p.m. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN formally adjourned the City Council
  meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
Deputy City Clerk  City Clerk

JULY 12, 2016
